messages.author: 5e9201f19b3ebb4b
messages.subject: Separate priors for different variables
parts:
Hello,
 first of all, thanks a lot for introducing rstanarm, it really makes running regression models very convenient. However, I have a question regarding priors - I would like to run a model in which each variable in X has a prior with different parameters. Is that possible? I have tried to input a list of priors with c(), but it seems to take into account only the first one. Thanks in advance!

Best regards,
 Marcel Falkiewicz

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Separate priors for different variables
parts:
On Sunday, June 19, 2016 at 1:05:14 PM UTC-4, Marcel Falkiewicz wrote:
 first of all, thanks a lot for introducing rstanarm, it really makes running regression models very convenient. However, I have a question regarding priors - I would like to run a model in which each variable in X has a prior with different parameters. Is that possible? I have tried to input a list of priors with c(), but it seems to take into account only the first one. Thanks in advance!

You can do different priors by specifying different hyperparameter values to a common distribution. For example, the normal() function accepts a vector for the location and the scale.

Ben

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Separate priors for different variables
parts:
As Ben said, you can pass vectors to many of the arguments to the functions used to specify priors. Just want to add that the order of the vector elements is the same as the order of the variables in the matrix given by passing your formula and data (or just a previous stanreg object for the same model) to model.matrix().

Jonah
